Passage 2 From the factory to your front door When you buy something from an e-commerce website, that thing takes a long journey before it arrives at
your home.

First, a company makes the product in a factory.
For example, imagine you buy a pair of shoes.
The shoes are first made in a factory.
After the workers finish making the shoes, they pack them into a box.
Then the company checks the quantity of products.
They count how many items are ready to sell and add this information to their inventory database.
Inventory helps the company know how many products are available and where they will be sent to the warehouse.
Next, your new shoes will leave the factory and move to a warehouse.
This step is called shipping.
Large trucks, ships, trains, or airplanes all transport products.
A warehouse is a big building where products are stored safely.
Workers organize the items on shelves and use databases to manage the warehouse inventory.
Warehouses are important because they keep products ready.
For customers.
The online purchase.
The shoes are now in the warehouse, waiting for you to buy them.
You go online, put them in.
In your virtual shopping cart, and you go to the checkout page.
There, you enter your billing and shipping information.
The e-commerce site creates an invoice.
An invoice is a document with information about the order, such as the product name, price, and quantity.
At checkout, you need to choose a shipping method.
Some people choose standard shipping because it costs less.
Others choose express shipping because it is faster.
You really want those shoes as soon as possible.
So you pay extra for express shipping.
The website usually shows the ETA or estimated time of arrival.
Your shoes will arrive in two days.
When you click the purchase button, the system in the warehouse adds the shoes to a list of purchased items and signals the workers in the warehouse to retrieve them.
The e-commerce site sends a receipt to you by email.
The receipt confirms that the payment was successful.
To the distribution center.
The warehouse workers prepare the order.
They find the product on the shelves, pack it carefully, and print a shipping label.
The shipping label includes your shipping address and zip code.
After packing, the product leaves the warehouse and travels to a distribution center, usually by truck.
A distribution center is different from a warehouse.
A warehouse stores products for a long time, but a distribution center moves products quickly.
At the distribution center, workers sort packages by city or region.
Machines and workers work together to organize thousands of boxes every day.
This step helps companies deliver products faster and more efficiently to your Front door.
After sorting, the package is loaded onto a delivery vehicle.
The delivery vehicle may be a van, truck, motorcycle, or bicycle.
Delivery drivers follow routes to bring packages to homes and offices.
Today, many companies use GPS to track deliveries, so you know how close your new shoes are to arriving.
Customers can often check the location of their package online and see updates about the ETA.
Finally, the delivery driver.
Driver arrives at your home.
